ann_30.text: This part acts on 157 of 242 training patients (65%), and 95 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.0 mm of ST depression and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG), it slightly raises the predicted risk, from about 99% to above 99% (on the training data only).

Through it, going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 25%, and a flat ST segment raises it from about 9% to about 14% (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: Through this part, non-anginal chest pain lowers a typical patient's predicted risk of heart disease from about 9% to about 2% (on the training data only).
It compares non-anginal chest pain with all other chest pain types taken together.

ann_32.text: This part acts on 49 of 242 training patients (20%), all of them patients with a normal resting ECG; 31 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with a normal resting ECG, 1.6 mm of ST depression, a flat ST segment and a reversible thallium defect), it changes the predicted risk only slightly, which stays at about 99% (on the training data only).
Through it, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 33% (on the training data only).

For patients with a normal resting ECG, ST depression adds risk here only once it rises above about 1.0 mm: for the typical patient with this bend (a 54-year-old man with a normal resting ECG and 0.4 mm of ST depression), going from 0 to 3.5 mm moves it from about 5% to about 36% (on the training data only).
Across the whole model, more ST depression clearly raises the predicted risk even more if the resting ECG is normal (from about 5% to about 69%, against about 5% to about 31% otherwise).
On its own through this part, the resting ECG changes the predicted risk only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: Through this part, going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 54% (on the training data only).
A higher maximum heart rate (118 to 175 beats per minute) lowers it only slightly through this part, from about 10% to about 8% (on the training data only).

ann_34.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (below 1%) or atypical angina (about 2%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 9%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 99%, a flat ST segment raises it to about 87%, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) from about 5% to about 69%, and a reversible defect or the undefined code 4 on the thallium scan to about 44% (on the training data only).

Higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises it from about 3% to about 28%, higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) from about 4% to about 20%, and chest pain brought on by exercise from about 9% to about 16% (on the training data only).
Being a woman lowers it from about 9% to below 1%, and a fixed defect on the thallium scan to about 1% (15 patients; the model has little data on this), both on the training data only.
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (to about 4%) and a maximum heart rate of 175 rather than 118 beats per minute (from about 10% to about 8%) lower it only slightly (on the training data only).
It ignores age.

ann_32.original: Hidden node 1801 = ReLU(1.48*restecg:0 + 0.805*oldpeak - 1.43), readout +1.335. ann_34.original: Root: output node 0 computes the logit z = -0.160 + LINEAR CORE + hidden readouts, and (binary task) the model applies a sigmoid at the output (get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU; decision is z>0). Children add: +0.983*ca_slope2_gate (near-affine in ca, slope:2), -1.305*cp3_affine_relay (affine, -0.66 cp:3), +1.669*2245 and -0.165*2009 from ca_thalach_chain (mostly affine: +1.30 ca, small -thalach), and +1.335*normal_ecg_st_gate (the one real interaction: oldpeak adds extra risk only when restecg:0=+1). ann_34.proposed: Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain and atypical angina lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. More vessels coloured, a flat ST segment, more ST depression, a reversible thallium defect, higher cholesterol, higher resting blood pressure and chest pain on exercise raise it; being a woman lowers it. summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk about 9%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (below 1%) or atypical angina (about 2%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 99%, and a flat ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 87% (on the training data only).

More ST depression on exercise raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: going from 0 to 2.8 mm clearly moves it from about 5% to about 69% with a normal resting ECG, and from about 5% to about 31% otherwise.
Being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to below 1%, and higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises it from about 3% to about 28% (on the training data only).

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to above 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 95 of these 157 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, for a typical patient, number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy going from 0 vessels to 2 vessels raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 9% to about 25% (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 14%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to about 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 31 of these 49 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, ST depression on exercise only adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 1.0 mm for patients with a normal resting ECG: for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves it from about 5% to about 36% (on the training data only).
